description:
Manage SQL, NoSQL and analytical databases in one app

DBine is a desktop database manager for relational, analytical, document, key-value, graph, time-series and search databases. One workbench connects to PostgreSQL, SQL Server, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, Oracle, MongoDB, Redis, Cassandra, ClickHouse, DuckDB, Snowflake, BigQuery, Elasticsearch, Neo4j, InfluxDB and many more engines.

Explore and query:
- A tree per connection and database, with saved queries kept inside each database
- A SQL editor with each engine's dialect, completion of tables and columns, and script execution
- A fast results grid with cell editing, filters, sorting, charts and a JSON tree view
- Graphical execution plans, a visual query builder and query optimization hints
- Search across object names, columns and stored code, and run code on several databases at once

Design and move data:
- Table designer, ER diagrams and script generation
- Compare schemas and data, then migrate, clone or sync databases between engines
- Import CSV, JSON, XLSX and XML; export results in many formats; generate test data and data subsets
- Rename objects with an impact analysis of everything that depends on them

Administer:
- Server monitor, live processes and a profiler of the queries clients run
- Users and permissions, backups, health checks and database properties
- SSH tunnels, including chains of bastions and the SSH agent
- Read-only connections and production safeguards

Assistant and integrations:
- An AI assistant that writes and explains queries with a local built-in model or Ollama; it never runs anything by itself
- A local MCP server so AI coding assistants can work with your connections, with every write approved in DBine
- End-to-end encrypted cloud sync of connections, queries and settings to your own account
- A script library and projects backed by git

Passwords are stored encrypted with a key kept in the system keychain, and never go into the state file or the logs.
DBine v1.3.0 installers.
New
- SSH tunnel profiles: save an SSH tunnel (server, bastions, user and authentication) once as a profile in Settings and pick it in any connection; each connection keeps its own database server. Editing the profile applies to every connection that uses it on its next connect, a connection's current tunnel can be saved as a profile, and the profile's secrets stay in the system keychain.
- Table columns on hover: resting the pointer on a table's name in the SQL editor shows its columns with their type, whether they allow nulls, the primary key and each column's comment, for every engine.
Improvements
- AI assistant with Claude Code and Codex: when you ask about another database on the same connection, the assistant reads its tables and columns without switching the tab's database. These models still never receive table rows.
Fixes
- SAP HANA on Linux, security: cancelling a query no longer reads the folder of trusted certificates after the session has removed it, a moment another user of the same computer could have used to plant their own certificate authority.
- Security, dependencies: ctutils and crypto-bigint are updated past their constant-time fixes.
- Excel export of very long text: a cell longer than Excel's limit is cut to fit again when it holds characters such as emoji, instead of stopping the export.
- Trino and Presto, security: copying or exporting data from a table whose column type is nested deeper than any real schema can no longer crash DBine; the depth limit added in 1.2.2 now covers that path too.
Thanks to @dylanwu, whose detailed reports led to the three new features in this release.
Downloads
- Windows: -setup.exe (requires WebView2, included in Windows 10/11).
- macOS: .dmg; aarch64 for Apple Silicon, x64 for Intel.
- Linux: .AppImage (portable), .deb or .rpm.
- Android: the phone app that pairs with DBine on your computer. Install it from dbine.com or with the -android.apk below; the first time, Android asks to allow installing apps from that source (the browser or the files app).
- Linux (Flatpak): .flatpak (x86_64 or aarch64), for flatpak install --user ./dbine-….flatpak; it doesn't update itself. Built by the flathub workflow, it appears here a while after the other files.
Version 0.1.4 and later receive it through the automatic update.
- macOS: signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple, so it opens without warnings.
- Windows: the -setup.exe installer is signed (Open Source Developer Marcos Panichella, Certum). While the certificate builds its reputation, SmartScreen may still ask for "More info" › "Run anyway".
- Each engine's driver (except SQLite) is downloaded the first time you connect.
